scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: One workstation in Campus 1 -- PC11, one of the
172.16.20.x machines -- has fallen off the network entirely. From that desk
you cannot reach anything: not the machines next to it, not the usual first
stop out, nothing at all. Every other desk around it is fine, and nothing
was moved or changed at that desk, so this is not something we did: the
network has dropped PC11 on your side. Look at why exactly that one machine
is cut off and put it back on today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I cannot reproduce the outage for PC11; the network side is healthy and forwarding correctly. Evidence:
- PC11’s NIC is up with 172.16.20.11/24 and a default route via 172.16.20.254. From PC11, ping to the gateway (172.16.20.254) succeeds with low RTT, and ARP shows the gateway MAC (00:01:97:e4:04:02) in REACHABLE state.
- Local L2 reachability works: other 172.16.20.x peers (e.g., PC9 and PC10) successfully ping PC11, and PC11 can ping them.
- Inter-VLAN routing works: PC11 successfully pings 172.16.10.5 in VLAN 10 through the routed “first hop out.”
- On switch2 (the access switch for VLAN 20), the bridge br_vlan20 has port eth5 in forwarding, and its FDB shows PC11’s MAC (32:08:af:52:b8:58) learned on eth5, confirming correct L2 attachment. The gateway MAC is present on the uplink subinterface eth0.20.

Affected component: none; all subsystems (L2 access on switch2, L3 gateway, ARP/forwarding) are operating normally. Mechanism: Because the switch has the correct MAC learning and ARP/GW reachability is intact, traffic to and from PC11 is being switched and routed as expected. Localization: PC11 on switch2.eth5, VLAN 20. Root cause: Issue is not present now; likely a transient endpoint-side condition (e.g., host NIC/cable or OS stack) rather than a network fault. Corrective fix: No network changes required; connectivity verified end-to-end. Recommend the helpdesk retest at the desk and, if symptoms recur, check the local NIC/cabling and capture exact time to correlate with port flaps.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254, same-VLAN hosts, and off-subnet destinations with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The writeup confirms successful gateway, intra-VLAN, and inter-VLAN pings but does not explicitly state 0% loss at baseline as required by this axis.

Minor truncation in the logs leaves one specific FDB line partially implicit, but overall the key claims are observable and the inferences are logical and complete.
